usage: the destination always takes 에, never 에서, when you simply 'go there'
get issued at the district office
the place where an action happens takes 에서; for documents like 건축물대장 you go to 구청, a simple 등본 is fine at the 동사무소
민원실 is the help-desk floor where you take a 번호표 and wait at a 창구
관할 (管轄) is the office responsible for your registered address; it matters when filing complaints
examples: 우리 동네 구청은 지하철역 바로 앞에 있어요.
Our neighborhood's district office is right in front of the subway station.
simple location sentence; note 구청 takes the topic/subject naturally without a counter
주차 단속 때문에 구청에 민원을 넣었어요.
I filed a complaint with the district office about parking enforcement.
민원을 넣다 'put in a civil request' is the set collocation for lodging a complaint
사업자등록은 구청 말고 세무서에서 해요.
You register a business at the tax office, not the district office.
real mix-up: 구청 handles residency and buildings, 세무서 handles taxes — '말고' means 'not X (but)'
nuance: 구청 (區廳, 區 'district' + 廳 'government office') is the borough-level city government serving an entire 구, one tier above the neighborhood 동사무소 and one tier below the city-wide 시청. As a resident you go there for ID and property documents, building paperwork, and parking or noise 민원. The dividing line learners blur is 구청 vs 시청 vs 동사무소: 시청 governs the whole city, 구청 one district inside it, 동사무소 one small neighborhood — so for an everyday 등본 the nearest 동사무소 is enough and you rarely need the 구청. The 廳 ending specifically marks a large administrative seat, which is why a small front desk is a 민원실, not a 구청. A pitfall for English speakers is treating 구청 like a generic 'city hall'; the precise English is 'district/borough office', and you must say 구청에 가다 (에, the goal), not 구청에서 가다.

Using 구청에서 가다 for 'go to the office'; the destination of 가다 takes 에 (구청에 가다). 에서 marks where an action is performed, e.g. 구청에서 서류를 떼다.
Going to 구청 for taxes; income and business taxes are handled at the 세무서, not the 구청.

usage: destination takes 에; 동사무소 is the smallest admin office, one per 동
get (a document) issued at the dong office
떼다 'tear off / pull' is the everyday verb for getting a certificate like 주민등록등본; 발급받다 is its formal twin
가깝다 (ㅂ-irregular: 가까운, 가까워요) describes the closest branch most residents use
usually weekdays 9 to 6; 영업시간 or 업무시간, closed weekends
examples: 등본 한 통만 떼러 동사무소에 잠깐 들렀어요.
I dropped by the dong office just to get one copy of my residence certificate.
통 is the counter for documents; 떼러 가다 'go in order to pull (a doc)' is the natural errand frame
요즘은 동사무소를 행정복지센터라고 불러요.
These days the dong office is officially called an administrative welfare center.
the modern name is 행정복지센터, but everyone still says 동사무소 — N(이)라고 부르다 'call it N'
이사하면 14일 안에 동사무소에서 전입신고 하세요.
When you move, file your move-in report at the dong office within 14 days.
전입신고 is legally required; late filing can mean a small fine
nuance: 동사무소 (洞事務所, 洞 'neighborhood' + 事務 'administrative affairs' + 所 'office') is the neighborhood-level office where residents handle the commonest errands: 전입신고 (move-in reports), 주민등록등본/가족관계증명서, and ID paperwork. Its official name was renamed 주민센터 and then 행정복지센터, yet spoken Korean overwhelmingly keeps 동사무소 — a good lesson that the textbook term and the street term diverge. The contrast to nail is 동사무소 vs 구청: the 동사무소 covers one 동 (neighborhood) and is closer and faster, the 구청 covers the whole 구 and handles weightier property/building matters. The 所 ending (also in 보건소, 파출소) marks a modest local 'station/post', unlike the grand 廳 of 구청. Pitfall: English speakers say 발급하다 ('to issue', what the office does) when they mean 발급받다 ('to be issued / receive'); a citizen 등본을 발급받다, the office 발급하다.

Assuming the self-service kiosk (무인발급기) is always free; a 등본 print is cheap or free, but you still must scan your ID to use it.

usage: go to the public health center
보건소 is a government-run clinic, typically one per district
get tested at the health center
검사받다 'undergo a test'; common for free or low-cost screenings and STI tests
get a vaccination / get a shot
the shot itself: 주사를 맞다 (lit. 'be struck by a shot') — never 주사를 받다
the health center for your area
관할 (管轄) is the one assigned to your district; it matters for some free programs
examples: 독감 주사 맞으러 보건소에 가요.
I'm going to the health center to get a flu shot.
주사를 맞다 is the fixed verb for receiving an injection; 맞으러 가다 'go in order to get (a shot)'
보건소에서 무료로 건강검진을 받을 수 있어요.
You can get a free health check-up at the public health center.
건강검진을 받다 'receive a health screening'; eligibility varies but basic ones are often free
독감 예방접종은 동네 보건소가 병원보다 훨씬 싸요.
The flu shot is much cheaper at the local health center than at a hospital.
보건소 vs 병원 — the budget motive; 보다 here marks the comparison standard ('than')
nuance: 보건소 (保健所, 保 'protect' + 健 'health' + 所 'office/station', literally a 'health-protection station') is the district-run public health center offering vaccinations, screenings, and basic care at little or no cost. The synonym line to learn is 보건소 vs 병원: a 병원 is a private hospital/clinic for diagnosis and treatment, while 보건소 is a public-budget facility for prevention and low-cost routine care — for a flu shot or travel vaccine you go to the 보건소, for a broken arm or surgery you go to a 병원. Its habitual partners are 예방접종, 건강검진, 무료, 검사. The register is neutral-administrative. Two pitfalls: (1) the shot collocation is 주사를 맞다 (passive 'be hit by an injection'), so the English 'get/receive a shot' must not become 주사를 받다; (2) don't confuse the local 보건소 with the national 보건복지부 (Health Ministry) — the ministry sets policy, the 보건소 is where you actually roll up your sleeve.

usage: 세무서 is the local branch of the national tax service (국세청)
file (a return) at the tax office
신고하다 (申告) 'declare/report' is the verb for income or a business registration; 에 marks where you report
your 관할 세무서 is decided by your business or home address
세금을 내다 'pay tax' vs 신고하다 'declare it' — declaring and paying are two separate steps
examples: 세무서가 어디에 있는지 아세요?
Do you know where the tax office is?
embedded question -는지; a gentle way to ask directions to the office
사업자등록증은 세무서에서 발급받았어요.
I got my business registration certificate from the tax office.
starting any business or side gig requires 사업자등록 at the 세무서; 발급받다 = receive (an issued doc)
프리랜서는 5월에 세무서에 종합소득세를 신고해야 해요.
Freelancers must file comprehensive income tax at the tax office in May.
May is 종합소득세 season; 신고하다 not 내다 — first you declare, then any tax due is paid
nuance: 세무서 (稅務署, 稅 'tax' + 務 'affairs' + 署 'bureau') is the local tax office, the branch of the national 국세청 where you do 사업자등록 and file income tax. The most dangerous confusion is the near-homophone pair 세무서 vs 세무사 (稅務士): 세무서 is the government office, 세무사 is a licensed private tax accountant you hire — one letter changes a public building into a paid professional. A second line is 신고하다 vs 내다: 신고 means to *declare/report* your income, while 내다 means to *pay* the resulting tax; you can 신고 without immediately 내다. Habitual partners: 종합소득세, 부가세, 사업자등록, 홈택스. Pitfall for English speakers: 'file taxes' should be 세금을 신고하다, but learners often borrow 'pay' for everything and say 세금을 내다 even when they only mean to submit the return. Also, don't go to the 구청 to register a business — that is squarely the 세무서's job.

Using 세금을 내다 ('pay tax') when you mean 신고하다 ('declare/file'); filing a return and paying the bill are distinct steps in Korean.

usage: 파출소 is the small neighborhood police post for minor matters
신고하다 'report (a crime/incident)'; for small incidents, lost items, or disputes
가깝다 → 가까운; they dot the neighborhoods, so one is usually close
hand (something) in at the police box
맡기다 'entrust/leave with' is the verb for turning in a found wallet
examples: 길을 잃으면 파출소에 가서 물어보세요.
If you get lost, go to the police box and ask.
simple safety advice; 파출소 doubles as a place to ask directions
지갑을 주워서 근처 파출소에 맡겼어요.
I found a wallet and handed it in at the nearby police box.
줍다 (ㅂ-irregular: 주워서) 'pick up'; 맡기다 'leave in someone's care' — the standard lost-and-found frame
밤에 취객이 시끄러워서 파출소에 전화했어요.
A drunk person was being loud at night, so I called the police box.
for non-emergency neighborhood trouble; -아서 gives the reason
nuance: 파출소 (派出所, 派 'dispatch' + 出 'send out' + 所 'post', literally a 'dispatch post' from which officers are sent into the neighborhood) is the small local police box you use for minor incidents, lost-and-found, and neighborhood disputes. The contrast to fix is 파출소 vs 경찰서 (警察署): the 파출소 is the tiny front-line post for everyday small matters, while the 경찰서 is the full district police station that investigates and processes formal cases — and for a genuine emergency you skip both and dial 112. A further wrinkle is that many 파출소 have been merged into larger 지구대 (地區隊) units, so older speakers say 파출소 where the sign now reads 지구대. Natural partners: 신고하다, 맡기다, 분실물, 순찰. Pitfall: English speakers treat 'go to the police' as one phrase, but Korean distinguishes the small 파출소 (walk-in, minor) from the big 경찰서 (formal cases) — and reporting urgent danger should be a phone call to 112, not a walk to the 파출소.

usage: 법원 is the courthouse where legal cases are heard
소송을 내다 'put forth a suit' is the everyday phrase; 제기하다 is the formal twin
판결 (判決) is the formal decision a judge issues; cf. 선고하다 'to hand down'
which 법원 hears your case depends on the address or contract terms
examples: 그 사건은 지금 법원에서 재판 중이에요.
That case is currently on trial at the court.
재판 중 'in the middle of trial'; 에서 marks where the proceeding happens
소액 사건은 법원에서 비교적 빨리 처리돼요.
Small-claims cases are handled relatively quickly by the court.
소액심판 is a simpler track; 처리되다 (passive) 'get processed'
집주인이 보증금을 안 줘서 법원에 소송을 냈어요.
The landlord wouldn't return the deposit, so I filed a lawsuit in court.
deposit (보증금) disputes are a common reason renters use the 법원; 소송을 내다 = file suit
nuance: 법원 (法院, 法 'law' + 院 'institution/hall') is the courthouse where civil and criminal cases are decided by judges. For an ordinary resident the realistic contact is a civil matter — most often recovering an unreturned 전세 or 월세 보증금 through a small-claims (소액심판) filing. The contrast to keep straight is 법원 vs 경찰서: the 경찰 (police) *investigate* and gather evidence, while the 법원 *judges* and rules — police never issue a 판결. Note also that 법원's product is a 판결 (ruling), not the same as a 합의 (private settlement). Habitual partners: 소송을 내다, 판결, 재판, 출석, 기한. A real pitfall: court documents carry strict deadlines (기한), and the English instinct to 'deal with it later' is dangerous — ignoring a 법원 letter can mean losing 'by default' (궐석/무변론 패소). Also use 에 for going (법원에 가다) but 에서 for the trial happening there (법원에서 재판하다).

usage: 체육관 is an indoor sports hall, often public and run by the district
구민 (區民) 'district residents'; these public halls are cheap to use
빌리다 'borrow' for casual use; 대관하다 (貸館) is the formal 'reserve the venue'
racket/court sports take 치다 'hit'; 운동을 하다 for exercise generally
examples: 주말마다 체육관에서 운동해요.
I work out at the sports hall every weekend.
마다 'every'; 에서 marks where the activity happens — a simple habit sentence
친구들이랑 체육관에서 배드민턴을 쳐요.
I play badminton with friends at the sports hall.
배드민턴/탁구/농구 take 치다; 이랑 'with' is the casual companion particle
구청에서 운영하는 체육관이라 이용료가 정말 싸요.
It's run by the district office, so the fee is really cheap.
public 체육관 vs private 헬스장 — the budget point; -(이)라(서) gives the reason
nuance: 체육관 (體育館, 體育 'physical education' + 館 'hall/large building') is an indoor gymnasium or sports hall, usually a public facility run by the 구청 or city, used for court sports, swimming, and group classes. The synonym you must separate is 체육관 vs 헬스장: a 체육관 is the *building/hall* for badminton, basketball, volleyball or a pool, whereas a 헬스장 (or 피트니스) is a private *weights-and-treadmill gym* — the English word 'gym' covers both, which is exactly the trap. The 館 ending marks a sizeable public hall (cf. 도서관 library, 박물관 museum), reinforcing that it is a venue, not a membership fitness room. Natural partners: 구민체육관, 실내, 대관, 예약, 이용료. Two pitfalls: (1) calling your weights gym a 체육관 sounds like a school sports hall — say 헬스장; (2) court sports use 치다 (배드민턴을 치다), not 하다, so 'do badminton' as 배드민턴을 하다 is understandable but less idiomatic.

usage: go to the public help desk
민원실 is the front-desk office for residents' requests inside a public building
민원을 넣다 'put in a civil request' is the everyday phrase; 제기하다 is formal
창구 (窓口) 'wicket/counter' is where you're served after taking a 번호표
처리하다 'process'; the office 처리하다, the citizen 넣다/제기하다
examples: 민원실이 몇 층에 있어요?
What floor is the help desk on?
층 'floor' with the question word 몇; a basic in-building direction question
서류 발급은 1층 민원실에서 번호표 뽑고 기다리세요.
For document issuance, take a number at the first-floor help desk and wait.
번호표를 뽑다 'pull a number ticket' is the standard 민원실 routine
주차 문제는 구청 민원실에 민원을 넣었어요.
I filed a complaint about parking with the district office help desk.
민원 covers complaints, not just document requests; 민원을 넣다 = lodge a request
nuance: 민원실 (民願室, 民 'people' + 願 'wish/petition' + 室 'room', literally the 'room for citizens' petitions') is the public-service desk inside a government building — the 구청, 동사무소, 세무서 etc. — where residents request documents or file complaints. The key insight is the root word 민원: it means a citizen's *formal request or grievance* to a public office, covering both neutral asks (issuing a certificate) and complaints (noisy construction). So the contrast to draw is 민원실 vs the building itself: 구청/동사무소 is the whole agency, while 민원실 is merely the 室 ('room') inside it where the public is served — it is a desk/floor, not a standalone building. The collocation engine: 민원을 넣다/제기하다 (lodge), 처리하다 (the office processes), 번호표를 뽑다, 창구. Pitfall: English speakers narrow 민원 to 'complaint', but a request for a 등본 is also a 민원; and don't say 민원실에 가다 expecting a separate address — it lives inside a larger 관공서.

usage: 등기소 handles official property and corporate registrations
떼다 is the everyday verb; 등기부등본 shows ownership and any 근저당 (mortgage liens)
등기 (登記) is the legal record of who owns a property
which 등기소 you use depends on the property's location
examples: 등기소는 보통 법원 근처에 있어요.
The registry office is usually near the courthouse.
true in practice (등기소 are tied to the court system); a simple location fact
요즘은 등기소에 안 가도 인터넷등기소에서 열람할 수 있어요.
These days you can view records on the internet registry without going to the office.
인터넷등기소 is the online portal; 열람하다 'inspect/browse (records)'
전세 계약 전에 등기부등본을 꼭 확인하세요.
Be sure to check the property register before signing a jeonse contract.
checking 등기부등본 reveals hidden mortgages before you pay a deposit; -기 전에 'before V-ing'
nuance: 등기소 (登記所, 登 'record/enter' + 記 'write down' + 所 'office', literally the 'recording office') is the registry that keeps official records of property ownership and company registration, administratively tied to the court (法院) system. Its single most practical product for a renter is the 등기부등본 — the property register you must read before signing a 전세 or 월세 contract to confirm the landlord truly owns the place and to spot existing loans (근저당권). The confusion to kill is the shared syllable 등기: 등기소/등기부 (property *registration*) is unrelated to 등기우편 (*registered* mail at the post office) — same 登記 'to record' but completely different services. Habitual partners: 등기부등본, 부동산 등기, 열람, 인터넷등기소, 근저당. Pitfall: English speakers skip the 등기부등본 check because 'the landlord seems nice', but verifying the register is the one concrete step that exposes a property already heavily mortgaged. Most people now 열람 online rather than visiting in person.

usage: 출입국사무소 handles visas and foreign-resident registration
체류 (滯留) 'stay/sojourn'; 연장하다 (延長) 'extend' — the core renewal phrase
get one's foreign resident card issued
외국인등록증 (ARC) is issued here; 발급받다 = receive (an issued doc)
the immigration office for your area
your 관할 office is set by where you live; reservations via 하이코리아
examples: 출입국사무소는 예약하고 가야 해요.
You have to make a reservation before going to the immigration office.
예약하고 가다 'reserve and (then) go'; walk-ins are limited
주소가 바뀌면 출입국사무소에도 신고해야 해요.
If your address changes you must report it to the immigration office too.
체류지 변경 신고 is required of foreign residents; 에도 'also to (there)' marks the extra place
비자 연장은 출입국사무소에 미리 예약하고 가야 해요.
For a visa extension you must book an appointment at the immigration office in advance.
walk-ins are hard; 하이코리아 reservations are expected; 미리 'in advance'
nuance: 출입국사무소 (出入國事務所, 出 'exit' + 入 'enter' + 國 'country' + 事務所 'office', literally the 'country-exit-and-entry affairs office') is the immigration office — the single most important 관공서 for a foreign resident. It issues the 외국인등록증 (ARC/foreign resident card), processes 비자 연장 (visa extensions) and changes of status, and records 체류지 변경 (address updates). Its formal current name is 출입국·외국인청 (the 廳-level seat), but the everyday term stays 출입국사무소. A useful pairing to know is 출입국사무소 vs 동사무소: when a foreign resident moves, the 동사무소 alone is not enough — the move must *also* be reported to 출입국, which is why Koreans say 출입국사무소'에도' 신고하다. Habitual partners: 예약, 하이코리아, 체류 연장, 외국인등록증, 발급받다. Pitfall: English speakers expect to walk in like at a US DMV, but most offices now require an online 하이코리아 reservation and may turn away walk-ins; and 비자 'visa' takes 연장하다 ('extend'), not the English-flavored 'renew' rendered literally.

usage: 우편함 is the box at your building where incoming mail lands
be slipped into / arrive in the mailbox
꽂히다 (passive) 'be stuck in' describes mail tucked into the slot
apartment lobbies have a wall of 공동 우편함, one slot per unit
many building 우편함 have a small dial/number lock
examples: 우편함에 편지가 왔어요.
A letter came in the mailbox.
오다 'come' is natural for mail arriving; 에 marks the location it landed in
관리비 고지서는 매달 우편함으로 와요.
The maintenance-fee bill comes to the mailbox every month.
우편함으로 오다 '(come) by way of the mailbox' — 으로 marks the route/channel; 고지서 = bills
등기우편은 우편함에 안 넣고 직접 받아야 해요.
Registered mail isn't left in the mailbox; you have to receive it in person.
등기 requires a signature, unlike regular mail; -지 않고 → 안 넣고 'without putting it in'
nuance: 우편함 (郵便函, 郵便 'mail/post' + 函 'box/case') is the *incoming* mailbox where letters and official notices are delivered, usually a locked unit in an apartment lobby. The crucial contrast is 우편함 vs 우체통 (郵遞筒): the 우편함 is your private *receiving* box at home, while the red 우체통 on the street is the public *outgoing* box you drop letters into — confusing them is the classic learner slip because English 'mailbox' covers both directions. (And 우체국 is the post office building itself.) Note 函 means a case/box, distinct from 통 'cylinder/bin'. Habitual partners: 확인하다, 고지서, 등기우편, 공동 우편함, 비밀번호; mail 'comes' to it via 우편함으로 오다. Pitfall: check it regularly, because 고지서 (bills), tax notices, and government letters with deadlines arrive here — and don't expect 등기우편 (registered mail) in the box, since registered items need an in-person signature and are otherwise re-delivered (재배송).

usage: 관공서 is the umbrella term for any public office (구청, 세무서, etc.)
업무 시간 (業務時間) usually weekdays 9 to 6, closed weekends and holidays
문을 닫다 'close (its) door' = be shut, esp. on 공휴일
official paperwork from a public office
documents issued or required by a 관공서
examples: 관공서는 주말에 문을 닫아요.
Government offices are closed on weekends.
문을 닫다 'shut the door' = be closed; a basic, high-frequency fact for newcomers
공휴일에는 관공서가 다 문을 닫아요.
On public holidays all government offices are closed.
공휴일 (public holiday) closures catch newcomers off guard; 다 'all'
관공서는 평일에만 열어서 점심시간에 다녀와요.
Government offices only open on weekdays, so I run over during lunch.
평일에만 'only on weekdays'; 다녀오다 'go and come back' for a quick errand
nuance: 관공서 (官公署, 官 'government/officialdom' + 公 'public' + 署 'bureau') is the general cover term for all government and public offices — the category that includes the 구청, 세무서, 동사무소, 보건소 and so on. The contrast to grasp is scope: 관공서 is the *umbrella word*, while 구청/세무서 are specific *instances* of it, so you use 관공서 when you mean 'public offices in general' (their hours, their closures) and the specific name when you mean one place. The practical knowledge baked into the word is the schedule: weekdays only, standard daytime hours (보통 9시–6시), and shut on 공휴일 — the set phrase being 관공서가 문을 닫다 ('the offices close their doors'). Habitual partners: 업무 시간, 공휴일, 휴무, 평일, 서류. Pitfall: English speakers assume offices keep bank-ATM-like evening or weekend access, but 관공서 generally close at 6 on weekdays and entirely on holidays — plan errands for a weekday morning, and use online services (정부24, 홈택스) when the office is shut.
